doc.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29

title: Would they choose music again
summary: The men say they have no regrets and would play until they cannot.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Gentlemen, one question we'll ask as a closer. If you had it all over again, would you go into music?
I would. I don't believe I would change anything.

In fact, I know I wouldn't. You mean if we would quit, if we would go back into it? Yeah, let's say you started over again, said okay you're 14 years old now. Would I start back again? You've got your life ahead of you, what are you going to be? Would I start? I want to learn how to play so much of music and tell her I look like music. That's right.

Well I'll tell you what myself. I wouldn't want to go back to London again, but it's principle I'd like to do what I'm doing right now, because I don't got that. Well that's what you mean, you had to start at 14 years old.
You had to go back to music again, start a new life.

Oh, well I just thought, I just thought, I was a man, I understand what I'm doing. I was a man in the service. I wouldn't know if I was a kid, 14 years old, I'd do it, but not like I was now. I wouldn't want it. No, no, I was not part of it, no, no. What I'm saying then is that you don't have any regrets. No, no, no, whatever. I wouldn't want it, I wouldn't want it.

The only way I'd stop playing music if I get sick and can't play no more, but as long as I'm feeling all right, and it's my power, the will of playing some music, I'm going to do that until Jesus Christ takes me out of the world. Yeah, and my... This? Mm-hmm. Oh, you want to hear that? Sure we do. Why? I'll try to make you hear it. Yeah. I know. You're not getting all of it. Glass of water, please. Certainly.
